description: Systematic approach to analyzing heart rate and rhythm patterns
overview: This module teaches the systematic approach to ECG interpretation, including rate calculation methods, rhythm assessment, and step-by-step analysis techniques.
objectives: Master different methods of heart rate calculation

slides.title: Rate Calculation Methods
slides.content: Three methods for rate calculation: 1) 300/R-R interval (large squares), 2) 1500/R-R interval (small squares), 3) Count R waves in 6 seconds × 10. Each method has advantages for different heart rates.

slides.title: Rhythm Regularity Assessment
slides.content: Assess rhythm regularity by measuring R-R intervals. Regular rhythm: variation <0.16s. Irregular rhythm: variation >0.16s. Patterns include regular, regularly irregular, and irregularly irregular.

quiz.question: How do you assess rhythm regularity?
quiz.explanation: Rhythm regularity is assessed by measuring R-R intervals between consecutive QRS complexes.

slides.title: Systematic Rhythm Analysis
slides.content: Systematic approach: 1) Rate, 2) Regularity, 3) P waves present?, 4) PR interval, 5) QRS duration, 6) Overall interpretation. This method ensures thorough and consistent analysis.

quiz.question: What is the first step in systematic rhythm analysis?
quiz.explanation: Rate calculation is the first step in systematic ECG rhythm analysis.

slides.title: Practice Cases
slides.content: Apply your knowledge to practice cases. Analyze different heart rates and rhythm patterns. Practice systematic approach with various clinical scenarios.

quiz.question: Which method is best for calculating heart rate in atrial fibrillation?
quiz.explanation: The 6-second count method is most accurate for irregular rhythms like atrial fibrillation.
